This course brings together the latest research on digital media and content creation and will provide students with a detailed understanding of the global media landscape.

Their study key aspects of the media industries, the changes and platforms that have emerged from digitalisation and how content is created across different media.

The course has a focus on understanding creativity and storytelling within all forms of media and how content creation, narrative and media audiences interact in contemporary media environments. Students will learn how stories are constructed across digital media platforms and how multimedia is understood by audiences.

Students will be drawn into a conversation about the international reach of digital media, and how convergence, globalisation and increasing platformisation have altered communications across cultures. The course looks in detail at several key media sectors and how they work, including the use of data platforms, convergence, audiences and semiotoics in contemporary digital media industries.

GCU’s innovative LLM in International Commercial Law is both research-led and informed by practice. It has been created with input from employers and students and draws on multi-disciplinary expertise across the Glasgow School of Business and Society.

Students will study as part of a diverse and engaged international cohort: there are no jurisdictional requirements and there is no expectation that students have already studied Law at undergraduate level.

The course has been carefully designed to appeal to future business leaders, finance professionals, or those who might already be working in a legal role or have undertaken some legal training.

Business, Economics and Law at Glasgow Caledonian University consistently rank highly in league tables and in the National Student Survey. By studying an LLM at Glasgow Caledonian University students will have an exceptional opportunity to become a business leader of the future.

Program Description

Strong financial management is vital to all organisations and the role of the accounting professional is complex, varied and subject to many different pressures. The MSc Accounting, Finance and Regulation course reflects this, covering not only the core areas of accountancy but also key financial and risk topics relevant to students' future career. Regulation is fundamental to accounting and finance and is a feature of many of the modules students will study.

This is an exciting time in the accounting profession with standards evolving and regulatory practices being reviewed and revised. As a student on the MSc Accounting, Finance and Regulation, students will develop a deeper academic and professional knowledge and understanding of the key challenges facing the accounting profession and the wider financial sector.

The accountancy team at Glasgow Caledonian University have a broad range of professional and academic experience which will enhance students' learning as a student on the course. Many of the accountancy academics students will meet have experience working in practice as professional accountants, across key areas such as financial reporting, management accounting, audit and the public sector.

An MSc Accounting, Finance and Regulation from Glasgow Caledonian University will provide students with the confidence and insight to develop their professional career or undertake further postgraduate academic study.

Please be advised that this is the fast track (8 month) option of the MSc Accounting, Finance and Regulation.

The Applied Business Analytics Master of Science programme at Glasgow Caledonian University is designed to prepare students for successful careers in the data-driven business world. It is particularly suited to individuals from business or non-technical backgrounds who wish to expand their expertise into analytics. Students gain sought-after skills in data analytics, visualisation, and programming, while also developing practical business abilities such as leadership and problem-solving.

The programme explores a range of analytical approaches, including identifying trends, forecasting outcomes, and making data-informed decisions. Teaching focuses on the application of analytical techniques to real business challenges, enabling students to put their learning into practice from the outset. The curriculum integrates technical competencies—such as artificial intelligence, programming, and data visualisation—with a strong emphasis on ethical data use, effective communication, and responsible leadership.

Upon completion, graduates will be able to:

  • Apply technical knowledge to real-world business challenges
  • Develop a strategic understanding of data use within legal and ethical frameworks
  • Lead analytics teams and manage data-driven projects
  • Build a strong foundation in programming, data storytelling, and decision-making through industry-standard tools such as Python, SQL, and Power BI.

Program Description

Environmental challenges require complex solutions, bringing together scientific, social, political and economic perspectives. GCU's MSc Environmental Management will provide students with the interdisciplinary perspective and diverse skillset to help solve environmental problems in a leadership role. Students can help their communities manage environmental concerns responsibly, making a positive impact and supporting the common good.

This degree course is accredited by the Chartered Institution of Water and Environmental Management (CIWEM), the Chartered Institution of Building Services Engineers (CIBSE) and the Chartered Institution of Wastes Management (CIWM). With the endorsement of four prestigious professional organisations, the MSc Environmental Management offers a respected credential that's relevant to employers around the world.

Students will have the option to complete a general course - giving them a broad understanding across a wide range of environmental disciplines - or choose among four pathways for specialisation.

  • Waste - As society strives to use resources more efficiently, we must ensure waste is properly and safely managed. Students will study sustainable waste management, contaminated land and landfill engineering, reuse and recycling in the manufacturing sector and more.
  • Energy - Global demand for energy has significant environmental implications, and renewable energy is just one part of a broader strategy. Students will explore energy technology, renewable energy, and building and energy performance.
  • Water - Communities depend on clean, plentiful water to survive, but there are water resource challenges around the world. Students will study treatment requirements for the water cycle, policy frameworks for managing supply, international policy, wastewater treatment and more.
  • Oil and Gas - Oil and gas operations pose environmental challenges, particularly off-shore operations. Students will learn about minimising the impact of emissions from oil production, exploring for oil and gas, and environmental regulations.

Delivered at Glasgow Caledonian University’s London campus, the Global MBA is built around a commitment to the Common Good and the United Nations Principles for Responsible Management Education (PRME).

The program is designed for enterprising and socially minded individuals aspiring to become professional managers with a strong focus on sustainable and socially responsible business practices.

The curriculum emphasizes leadership development through innovation and creative thinking, preparing graduates to lead effectively in a rapidly evolving global environment. Upon completion, graduates are equipped to identify their own professional development needs and demonstrate the attributes of responsible leadership.

The flexible structure of the MBA allows for specialization through a choice of nine elective modules, with the option to graduate with an MBA (Public Health) or an MBA (Insurance) by selecting pathway-specific modules.

This applied and practice-oriented program provides insight into the real-world challenges faced by managers across business and third-sector organizations worldwide. It highlights the integration and strategic contribution of core business functions, strengthening the ability to design and implement effective, organization-wide strategies.

The course fosters an engaging and collaborative learning environment, bringing together ambitious and highly motivated peers, and offers access to a global alumni network of socially responsible leaders. Glasgow Caledonian University London attracts a diverse international student body and delivers a strong student experience with a focus on global employability and leadership across sectors.

This MBA course has been designed around GCU's commitment to the Common Good and the UN Principles for Responsible Management Education (PRME). This distinctive MBA course is designed for enterprising and socially minded individuals with aspirations to become a professional manager with an instinct for creating sustainable business in a socially responsible manner.

This practical and applied course provides insight into the everyday challenges confronting managers within a range of business and third sector organisations across the globe. Emphasis is place on the role, contribution and integration of the key business functions to enhance students' abilities to design and deliver effective organisation-wide strategies.

Dynamic and challenging, the MBA requires energetic participation. MBA students are ambitious, highly-motivated and determined to succeed. Students are welcomed onto the program and into GCU's global alumni network of socially responsible leaders.

The Global MBA course provides sessions on contemporary issues such as

  • Dealing with Black Swan Events (such as COVID-19) and Scenario Planning
  • Crisis Leadership
  • Business Continuity in Uncertain times
